newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks focused on banks, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks focused on banks, Wall St.

text.p: More volatile trading is likely for Hong Kong stocks in the week ahead, with investor attention split between Wall Street and the local banking sector in the run-up to the reporting season, brokers said.

"We may track Wall Street next week, although the focus will also be on the (local) banking sector," said Lino Delgado, associate director at Amsteel Securities. "Liquidity is still very high so we could have more volatile trading."
The Hang Seng Index dipped sharply in late Friday trade to close down 135.89 points, or 0.87 percent, at 15,570.40 on turnover of HK$20.82 billion ($2.7 billion).
Over the week, the index gained 2.27 percent.
Most brokers see the index consolidating in the week ahead, but caution that much will depend on HSBC Holdings.
Hong Kong's performance last week was roughly in line with Wall Street's but with local factors the driving force.
The Hang Seng set records throughout the past week, reaching an all-time high of 15,783.27 on Thursday, fueled by a rally in both HSBC and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.
The Dow Industrials powered to an all-time high of 8,069.77, then eased to a record closing high of 8,038.88 on Wednesday, following a tame consumer price report for June.
But the Wall Street barometer reversed course on Thursday, slipping 18 points, then tumbling another 130 points on Friday.
"At these levels we are likely to see further gyrations, more volatility," said Amsteel's Delgado.
Brokers were divided on the outlook for HSBC Holdings, which has been largely responsible for the Hang Seng's currently lofty levels.
The share surged HK$15.00 on Thursday to a record high of HK$279.00 then lost most of that rise on Friday when it shed HK$14.00 to close at HK$265.00.
"HSBC has met its target of HK$265.00 for the year," said Mark Coggins, head of Hong Kong research at NAVA SC Securities.
"We are not going to see the market surge ahead next week," Coggins said. "Unless and until we see faster loan growth, the banking sector is pretty fairly valued."
Others disagree.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see earnings growth of 15 percent to 20 percent for first-half earnings, the top end of expectations," said Delgado.
Earnings forecast for the banking giant range from six percent growth to 20 percent. HSBC Holdings and its subsidiary Hang Seng Bank Ltd will report interim earnings on August 4.

In the coming week, Hongkong Telecom will continue to attract attention due to expectations of greater opportunities in China and that a Chinese institution will seek a greater stake in the company, brokers said.
But after its recent breakout of a 3-1/2 year trading range, some analysts believe the share has limited near-term upside.

"Hongkong Telecom is trading well above its fair value," said Coggins. The share set an all-time high on Friday of HK$20.40, then eased slightly to close HK$1.05 higher on the day at a record closing high of HK$20.15.
Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels will report first-half results on Thursday and China Light and Power its third-quarter results on Friday. ($ = HK$7.749)
